title: Conversational salience extractor for KV slimming and cache prioritization
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Problem: The runtime's KV cache stores full per-prefix KV blobs which drive GPU memory residency and reduce effective throughput under heavy multi-tenant conversational workloads. Many tokens in long conversational contexts contribute little to future token prediction (low salience), yet occupy slots in the cached KV slabs. This ticket explores building a lightweight salience extractor that identifies high-impact tokens/prefix segments and produces a compact 'slimmed' KV anchor representation to: (1) reduce per-request GPU KV resident size, (2) keep high cache hit rates across similar prompts, and (3) preserve end-user quality.

Goal: Implement a runtime-level salience scoring and KV slimming pipeline that can be toggled by feature flag and validated via canary. The system must maintain latency SLOs and produce measurable GPU memory reduction while keeping quality regressions under an agreed threshold.
acceptance_criteria: Slimmed KV representation reduces average GPU-resident KV memory per active slot by >= 25% on the conversational benchmark (internal convbench-v2)
End-to-end generation quality (ROUGE-L / embedding distance on evaluation set) degrades by <= 2% relative to baseline for the slimmed mode
Per-request added CPU/host-latency before batching < 4ms P95
Cache hit rate for repeated/consecutive prompts improves or is neutral compared to baseline (>= 0% change), demonstrating effective reuse
Feature gated and rolled out to 5% canary with monitoring and automatic rollback on defined alerts
implementation_plan: Design a token/prefix salience heuristic (two-stage): fast heuristic using next-token logits + token-level surprisal, fallback to a tiny distilled salience network for ambiguous cases
Define compact KV anchor format: ordered list of (anchor-token-hash, relative-position, compressed-kv-snapshot) with a tunable granularity parameter
Integrate salience extractor into the request preprocessor: compute salience for incoming prefixes, produce slim-key for KV lookup and slimmed-KV for GPU residency
Modify KV store read path to accept anchors and perform partial expand-on-demand to rebuild transient KV for generation when needed
Add metrics hooks and feature flagging in Console (canary controls, per-tenant toggle)
Implement A/B experiment harness and synthetic replay tests using convbench-v2 workload generator
Create runtime e2e tests, microbenchmarks and GPU OOM regression tests
Ship PRs incrementally: salience heuristic -> anchor format -> runtime integration -> rollback safe canary
milestones: M1: Design doc + spike salience heuristic (2025-11-18)
M2: Anchor format and unit tests merged (2025-11-24)
M5: Gradual rollout plan or rollback (2025-12-15)
design_decisions: Use a two-stage salience approach: cheap heuristic to cover ~90% of prefixes, small (<=1M params) distilled model for edge cases
Anchor format will be content-addressed (hash+metadata) to allow cross-tenant reuse where permitted
Perform lazy re-expansion of slimmed KV on GPU only when generation path requires omitted low-salience parts
Quantize distilled salience model to int8 to meet the <4ms preprocess latency target
Keep original full-KV as a fallback object in the KV store for backward compatibility and A/B validation
risks: Quality regression for prompts that rely on low-salience but semantically important tokens (false negatives)
Added CPU overhead under extreme read-heavy workloads may increase host contention
Complexity in cross-tenant anchor reuse may introduce data isolation concerns (must ensure no cross-tenant leakage)
Edge cases where lazy re-expansion causes tail latency spikes if expansion occurs during hot-path generation
